harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created locked-password opsbot accounts on both nodes. Node1 now holds a protected ED25519 key that authenticates opsbot to node2. SSH requires public-key authentication for opsbot on both systems, while existing root policy remains unchanged. Both nodes restarted sequentially and fully recovered with new boot identities. OS, kernel, and OpenSSH versions were preserved.
actions_performed: Created opsbot accounts and restricted SSH directories on both nodes.
Generated the private key on node1 and installed only its public key on node2.
Added and validated an opsbot-scoped SSH configuration requiring publickey authentication.
Verified node1-to-node2 command execution as opsbot and rejection of password-only authentication on both nodes.
Restarted node1 and node2 one at a time and verified persistent configuration and functionality.
Removed temporary probes and confirmed no failed systemd units.

evidence.summary: Shows locked accounts, restrictive permissions, node1 key creation, and the matching public key authorized on node2.

evidence.requirement: Key-only authentication for opsbot on both systems
evidence.summary: Effective SSH policy requires publickey for opsbot; password-only attempts were denied on both nodes.

evidence.requirement: node1 opsbot can execute commands as opsbot on node2
evidence.summary: The intended workflow executed on node2 as opsbot before and after both node restarts.
Healthy baseline, acknowledged safe reboot, changed boot identity, and recovered SSH, account data, key access, checksums, and security policy.
Healthy baseline, acknowledged safe reboot, changed boot identity, and recovered SSH, account data, authorized key, checksums, and security policy.

evidence.requirement: OS/kernel preservation, administrative-policy preservation, and cleanup
evidence.summary: RHEL release, kernel, and OpenSSH package versions remain unchanged; root SSH policy is unchanged, temporary files are absent, and no failed units remain.
